newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela taps private firms to boost oil output.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela taps private firms to boost oil output.

text.p: Production from oil fields operated by private companies should account for a third of Venezuela's total production by the year 2006, an executive of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA said on Wednesday.

Including a sharp boost in production from fields offered up in the June lease round, private operators should pump an estimated 2.4 million barrels per day of the country's expected 6.3 million barrel per day output by 2006, Juan Szabo, PDVSA exploration and production coordinator, said.
"In Venezuela, one third of production will be by private operators by 2006," he said at an energy conference here.

Venezuela expects production from 20 areas offered in its upcoming third round to jump to about 400,000 barrels per day by 2006 from the current 70,000 barrels per day. Those fields hold an estimated 22 billion barrels of oil in place, of which 2.5 billion barrels have been produced to date, he said.

Szabo said 200 companies were prequalified of 350 companies interested in bidding in the country's third round on producing fields slated for reactivation. Bidding opens June 2 on five areas open only to domestic companies, he said.

Companies operating fields offered in the country's first two lease rounds are expected to boost production in those fields to 400,000 barrels per day in 2006 from 260,000 barrels per day currently, he said.
Fields operated under strategic association and production-sharing contracts are expected to produce about 1.7 million barrels per day by 2006, he said.

Overall, Venezuela plans to boost total domestic production to 6.3 million barrels per day in 2006 from 3.7 million barrels per day expected this year, he said. Including its share from fields operated by private companies, PDVSA will account for 4.4 million barrels per day in 2006, he said.

Private investment has fueled much of the production growth estimates, with private companies expected to spend up to $31 billion on exploration and production in Venezuela during the next ten years, he said.

Currently, 46 private companies are operating alongside state-owned companies in the country's oil industry. "The oil industry has certainly changed in Venezuela, and it has changed for the better," Szabo said.
